extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships (internationally mobile postdoctoral researchers in the life sciences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines describing how EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowship applications are screened, pre‑screened and interviewed, and which applicant, project and host‑lab factors the Fellowship Committee uses when making final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and eligibility check
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications are initially reviewed by the EMBO Fellowships Office for completeness and eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first filter applied to every submission; ineligible or incomplete applications are removed before committee pre‑screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑screening using condensed application form
rubrics_metrics.description: All eligible applications are then sent to the Fellowship Committee for pre‑screening, and about twice the number of available fellowships are selected for an interview (~25% of applications). During the pre‑screening, the committee reviews a condensed application form, which includes a summary of the applicant’s main scientific achievements along with the three most important publications, summary and biological significance of the proposed work, justification for choice of the host lab, as well as reference and acceptance letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The condensed form content (achievements, top 3 publications, project summary and significance, host lab justification, reference and acceptance letters) is the material used for pre‑screening; roughly 2× oversubscription is used to decide who progresses to interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous scientific achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous scientific achievements of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated via the applicant’s summary of achievements and the three most important publications supplied in the application. Past performance is a formal selection dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and biological significance of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty and biological significance of proposed research. Applications to continue exploring a topic similar to the PhD project usually receive lower priority for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee gives weight to how novel and biologically significant the proposed project is; continuation of very similar work from a PhD is a negative signal (lower priority). The condensed project summary and its stated biological significance are used to judge this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of the host laboratory for the proposed research and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of the host laboratory for the proposed research and training of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must justify their choice of host lab; the committee assesses whether the host environment can deliver the proposed training and project. Acceptance letters and the host justification in the condensed form are evidence for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and acceptance letters as supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference and acceptance letters are part of the condensed application materials reviewed during pre‑screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These letters serve as supporting evidence for applicant quality and host lab commitment; they are considered during pre‑screening and (if no interview possible) during written evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview evaluation by subject‑matter expert (or written evaluation alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants who successfully passed the pre‑screening, an interviewer with expertise in the area of the application will be selected from among the EMBO Members and EMBO Young Investigators. When it is not possible to arrange a personal or video interview, the candidate’s application is sent for written evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are conducted remotely via videoconferencing and last 90 minutes. The interviewer is an expert in the applicant’s area and will evaluate the candidate (the applicant is responsible for contacting the interviewer). If interview cannot be arranged, evaluation is based on the written application. Interviews normally take place within six to twelve weeks of the evaluation deadline and are a decisive stage before final committee decisions.
